formula_checks.name: earmarkedKinds
formula_checks.why: Excluding property and keeping only accounts with an earmarked amount above zero is right, and 'no kind = other' is reasonable. But the formula never says how the earmarked amount is worked out when the person left the earmark blank. The type says a blank earmark means 'use the default share for that kind', yet the formula only says 'earmarked amount above zero'. Read literally, a blank earmark gives zero and a 401(k) the person never touched drops out of the benchmark editor.
formula_checks.should_be: Earmarked amount = balance × (the person's earmark % if entered, otherwise the default share for that kind) ÷ 100. List each distinct kind among non-property accounts whose earmarked amount is above zero; an account with no kind counts as 'other'.
formula_checks.rests_on: The AssetAccount type: retirement_pct null/absent = use earmarkDefault; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: assetsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: The 'savings or portfolio' answer is always filed as taxable stocks and funds with a 7% target return. A household that answers with its savings — cash in a bank — gets that cash projected to grow at 7% a year as if it were invested in stocks. The 7% stock assumption is applied to money it should not touch.
formula_checks.should_be: Map 'savings' to a cash account with the app's cash return assumption (not 7%), and only a portfolio answer to taxable stocks and funds at 7%. If one setup question cannot tell savings from a portfolio, split it into two questions or ask which it is; do not default cash into stocks.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard practice: cash and equities carry different expected returns; the cash return assumption is far below a 7% equity assumption.

formula_checks.name: getAssetsState
formula_checks.why: It returns nothing when no accounts are saved, but is silent on a saved record whose account list is empty (everything deleted). If that is passed to buildAssetsState it returns a total of 0 and an invented 7% blended return — a default number where the honest answer is 'no answer'.
formula_checks.should_be: Return nothing when there is no saved record OR the saved account list is empty; otherwise return buildAssetsState of the accounts.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: a default number invented where the honest answer is 'no answer'; buildAssetsState's 7% fallback.

formula_checks.name: correctClassOf
formula_checks.why: A money market account is sent to Stocks / Funds. A bank money market deposit account is an FDIC-insured bank deposit, and a money market fund is a cash equivalent; both are cash, not stocks. Filing them as Stocks / Funds overstates the stock share of the mix and pulls the wrong return assumption onto cash.
formula_checks.should_be: Name evidence first; else Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date; else Cash for a money market account or fund; else Bonds & CDs for a CD; else nothing.
formula_checks.rests_on: FDIC: money market deposit accounts are insured deposits; FASB ASC 230 treats money market funds as cash equivalents.

formula_checks.name: reclassifyAccounts
formula_checks.why: Two gaps. (1) The person's own asset-class answer is one of its inputs, yet the formula overwrites any account whose class differs from correctClassOf — including one the person set themselves and confirmed. (2) It does not say what counts as one change: an account whose class and tax bucket both change, and holdings inside it, could be 1, 2 or more.
formula_checks.should_be: Skip any account whose class (or tax bucket) the person set and confirmed. Count one change per account or holding whose class actually changed; say explicitly whether the tax-bucket flip is counted separately (it should not be — it is part of the same correction).
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own input MK-XS-I-048 (the person's own asset-class answer); the type's rule that a user-confirmed wrapper is never overridden.

formula_checks.name: bondInfo
formula_checks.why: 'A missing figure counts as zero.' A bond with no coupon rate entered then shows a 0.00% current yield instead of a dash, and a CD entered with only a balance (no face value) gets face 0, which makes approxYTM a large negative yield. Accrued interest is rightly kept as 'not entered'; face, rate and value need the same treatment.
formula_checks.should_be: Copy each figure as entered; keep face value, coupon rate and maturity as 'not entered' when missing (as accrued interest already is), so that each downstream figure refuses rather than computing from an invented zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: something missing counted as zero; standard yield formulas are undefined without a face value or coupon.

formula_checks.name: annualCoupon
formula_checks.why: Annual coupon is face value × coupon rate; price does not enter it. The zero-for-missing problem sits in bondInfo (MK-NW-F-056), not here.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard bond definition: coupon = par × coupon rate.

formula_checks.name: yearsToMaturity
formula_checks.why: Days ÷ 365.25, floored at zero, with no answer for an invalid date, is a standard approximation. A maturity exactly one year away comes out at 0.9993 rather than 1, which no person will see once shown to one decimal.

formula_checks.name: currentYield
formula_checks.why: Current yield is annual coupon ÷ clean price. Subtracting accrued interest (when known) from a dirty value gives the clean price, and refusing when that is zero or less is right.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard definition of current yield (coupon ÷ clean market price).

formula_checks.name: approxYTM
formula_checks.why: The approximation itself is the standard one. But it uses the bond's value as entered, which includes accrued interest, while currentYield (MK-NW-F-059) subtracts accrued interest first. The two yields shown for one bond are worked on different prices; with accrued interest of $412 on a $25,000 bond the YTM falls from about 4.57% to 3.76%.
formula_checks.should_be: (Yearly coupon + (face − clean price) ÷ years left) ÷ ((face + clean price) ÷ 2), where clean price = value − accrued interest when entered. Refuse with no maturity date, when matured, or when clean price is zero or less.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard approximate YTM formula, priced on clean price; consistency with MK-NW-F-059.

formula_checks.name: bondSummary
formula_checks.why: Average yield = total coupon ÷ total value uses dirty values (accrued interest included), while currentYield (MK-NW-F-059) uses clean value. The summary's 'average yield' therefore disagrees with the value-weighted average of the per-bond current yields it sits above. Next maturity, counts and totals are right; 'not passed' correctly keeps a bond maturing today.
formula_checks.should_be: Average yield = Σ(face × rate) ÷ Σ(value − accrued interest where entered); nothing when that divisor is zero or less. Label it as an average current yield, not yield to maturity.
formula_checks.rests_on: Consistency with MK-NW-F-059; value-weighted average of current yields = Σcoupon ÷ Σclean value.

formula_checks.name: couponIncomeAnnual
formula_checks.why: For a bond or CD with no face value entered (a CD typed in with just its balance and rate is common), this gives face × rate = 0, while interestIncomeAnnual (MK-NW-F-063) falls back to balance × rate for the same account. Two formulas for the same interest disagree, so the Bonds screen shows less interest than the income figure.
formula_checks.should_be: Over bonds and CDs: face × rate when both are set; otherwise balance × rate when a rate is set; otherwise nothing — the same per-account rule as MK-NW-F-063.

formula_checks.name: interestIncomeAnnual
formula_checks.why: The per-account rules are sensible, but the formula is silent on a bond or CD that has already matured and is still listed: it keeps counting a year's interest that will never be paid. It is also silent on the uninvested cash inside a brokerage (cash_balance), which usually earns sweep interest.
formula_checks.should_be: As written, but count nothing for a bond or CD whose maturity date has passed; say explicitly whether a brokerage's cash sleeve with a stated rate is included.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary finance: a matured bond pays no further coupons.

formula_checks.name: bondRateSensitivity
formula_checks.why: Three faults. (1) The change is measured as priceAtYield(new yield) − today's value. priceAtYield rounds the years to a whole number, so even at the current yield it does not reproduce today's value; the 'change' then mixes the rate move with that model error (a 4.4-year discount bond shows +$2,000/−$1,000 where the rate effect is about +$1,760/−$1,680). (2) Rounding the range and the change to the nearest $1,000 erases the answer for an ordinary bond: a $10,000 bond shows '$10,000–$10,000' and a change of $0. (3) The figure must refuse for a CD (founder, 2026-09-27), but nothing in the formula checks for a CD, and BondInfo carries no kind, so a CD gets an estimate. Owner rule DEC-0071 (donut labels) has nothing to do with this figure.
formula_checks.should_be: Refuse for a CD, a matured bond, no coupon, or no maturity. Let y = approximate YTM. Change for a move of ±1 point = priceAtYield(y ± 0.01) − priceAtYield(y) (both on the same whole-year grid). New value = today's value + change. Range = new value × 0.99 to × 1.01. Round to a precision that scales with the bond (e.g. nearest $10, or three significant figures), not a fixed $1,000.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard practice: measure a price change with the same model at both yields; founder 2026-09-27 on CDs; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: buildNetWorth
formula_checks.why: Net worth = total assets − total debt, returned with both totals, is the definition.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; definition of net worth.
